title: Change the jurisdiction, recheck the rule
subtitle: Compare a fictional Australian kettle file with its own authority.
summary: Compare a fictional Australian kettle file with its own authority. Identify what a borrowed UK timing card cannot establish.
audience: General readers; all selected evidence and task instructions are included.
scope: Pinned Australian federal compilation 167 of 16 September 2026 and ACCC guidance, not a complete NSW legal decision. State procedure, commencement effects and individual entitlements are outside the exercise.

passages.title: Pinned authority
passages.text: The selected compilation separates guarantee questions from remedies. Sections 259–263 distinguish repairable non-major failures, major failures and restrictions on rejection. Section 262 uses a contextual rejection period; a UK thirty-day card does not supply its rule.
passages.context: Original bounded summary of the dated source reading; see source scope and limits.

passages.title: Guidance has a different role
passages.text: ACCC guidance explains major/minor problems and remedies. The agency states that it does not resolve individual disputes or give case-specific advice. Guidance is distinct from the statute and from a ruling.
passages.context: Original bounded summary of the dated source reading; see source scope and limits.

passages.title: Fictional transaction and variants
passages.text: A NSW household buys a new kettle for domestic use from an incorporated retailer, without an auction, resale purpose or finance. Variant A stipulates an unsafe concealed fault. Variant B stipulates an easily repairable non-major fault. Variant C records several failures but leaves their combined significance disputed.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

passages.title: An inserted card
passages.text: A note in the file says: thirty days after delivery, because that was the rule in an earlier UK exercise. It supplies no Australian statutory locator.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

lenses.label: Name the authority
lenses.observation: The transaction and compilation are explicit, while the inserted timing card has no Australian basis.
lenses.question: What would be needed to justify a local rejection-period conclusion?
readings: Identify the applicable provision and the facts it makes relevant.
Keep a separate list of unverified state, procedure and legal-effect questions.
lenses.boundary: Do not calculate an Australian deadline from the UK example.

lenses.label: Compare the stipulated variants
lenses.observation: The variants alter the failure description, not the governing country.
lenses.question: Which condition still needs analysis in each variant?
readings: For B, inspect the supplier-remedy stage and consequences of refusal or failure within reasonable time.
For C, examine the statutory combined-failures test; counting failures alone is insufficient.
lenses.boundary: The exercise supplies branch-reading questions, not a resolved personal claim.

lenses.label: Keep guidance and adjudication separate
lenses.observation: A regulator explanation is available; a ruling on this fictional file is not.
lenses.question: What claim would require evidence beyond the public guidance?
readings: An outcome for an individual dispute needs its facts and applicable legal analysis.
A current legal-effect claim needs the relevant amendments and application rules.
lenses.boundary: An official source is not automatically a complete answer to every case.

activity.transfer: Remove the foreign timing card. Replace it with the jurisdiction, pinned compilation, provision to inspect and two missing facts. Explain why a structurally similar problem can need a different legal analysis.
rubric: Identify authority before importing a rule.
Separate a guarantee, failure classification and remedy restrictions.
Do not turn several faults into an automatic major-failure finding.
Preserve the boundary between guidance and a case decision.
